Full release notes: **https://danbyte.net/news/v0-16-0**

### New in 0.16.10

#### Added

- **VMware Cloud Director sync.** A third virtualization connector, behind its own **Cloud Director sync** switch under Settings → Integrations. One source is one organization: the org becomes a **cluster group**, each Org VDC a **cluster**, each vApp a **VM group**, and every machine a **virtual machine** with its interfaces and addresses. Test connection reports the API version the two sides agreed on. This first release is for the field: it is written against a real 45-VM sample and a working reference script, but it has not yet been run against a live appliance. (#98)
- **The API version is negotiated rather than configured.** Cloud Director publishes the versions it speaks; Danbyte reads that list and uses the newest one this release was tested against, which is **38.1**. An appliance ahead of Danbyte still syncs, on a version both sides know, and the source page says so. One below the **36.0** floor is refused by name instead of failing on a payload it cannot read. A version can be pinned per source to work around a specific appliance.
- **VM groups.** A named set of virtual machines below a cluster - a Cloud Director vApp today, and the same shape a Proxmox resource pool or a vCenter folder would take. A cluster page lists its groups, a VM's Overview names the one it is in, and the sync fills a blank group but never replaces one you set by hand.
- **External addresses can become NAT rules.** Off by default: a Cloud Director VM reporting a translated address writes a static NAT rule for it, outside and inside. The rule carries no device, because the translation happens on an edge gateway an organization account cannot see, and both addresses still have to fall inside a prefix you already model.

#### Changed

- **A guest is now tracked by whichever identity its hypervisor uses.** Proxmox and vCenter keep their integer id; Cloud Director has only a UUID, which does not fit in the field the other two use. The sync pass and its pruning key on the guest record itself, so neither connector has to know about the other's column.
- **Two machines of one name on a single hypervisor are reported, not merged.** Cloud Director scopes a VM name to its vApp while Danbyte scopes it to the tenant, so the second machine was silently adopted onto the first one's record and the two then fought over its specs every pass. The second is now skipped and named on the Last sync badge.
- **A synced cluster is typed after the hypervisor it came from.** An unknown connector used to fall through to a *Proxmox VE* cluster type, which labelled a VMware cluster as Proxmox with no sign anything was wrong.
- **The virtualization source dialog is driven by a per-hypervisor table** rather than a vCenter flag, so ports, placeholders, credential wording and the optional switches all come from one place.
